transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what's brought you in?

Hi, yeah, thank you. Um... so, I guess what finally pushed me to actually make this appointment—and actually show up to it, which honestly is a miracle in itself lately—is that I am just completely failing at, like, basic adult things. I recently finished my bachelor's, so I'm supposed to be getting my life together and entering the real world, but I keep forgetting literally everything. 

And I don't mean just silly little things, I mean really important stuff, like paying my bills. I'll get a bill in the mail, put it on the kitchen counter, tell myself I'll log on and pay it right after dinner, and then it just completely vanishes from my reality until I get slapped with a huge late fee or a shut-off notice. 

But the really scary part, and why I realized I had to talk to someone, is that it's starting to cost me real, actual opportunities. Like, I'm trying to get a job right now since I don't have one, but I keep forgetting to return interview emails. I'll read an email from a recruiter on my phone, think, "Oh, I need to sit down at my laptop and draft a really professional reply to this," and then I just... don't. A week or two will go by, I'll suddenly remember in the middle of the night, and by then the job is totally gone. They've moved on to someone else. 

It's the same with showing up for appointments, I just completely blank on them unless someone is physically dragging me there. Or even just following through on basic errands, like dropping off a package or going to the bank. I'll leave the house specifically to do an errand and somehow come back hours later having done absolutely everything except the one thing I left to do. It's just... it's so frustrating because I know what I'm supposed to be doing, but my brain just drops these really basic responsibilities, and my life is just totally stalling out because of it.
Did you notice this kind of forgetfulness and trouble following through on tasks back in childhood or school, or is this something that's really only become a problem recently?

Oh, gosh, no, it's definitely not new. It's... it's been happening forever, honestly. Like, I remember even way back in elementary school, my parents used to get so frustrated because every single parent-teacher conference was the exact same conversation. The teachers would always say, you know, "She's so bright, she has so much potential, she understands the material," but then in the very next breath, it was, "But she constantly loses her worksheets." And it was true! I would do the homework—well, sometimes I would do the homework—and then I would just shove it into my desk or my backpack, and it would vanish into another dimension. 

My desk was a complete disaster zone. I mean, it was legendary how messy it was. I could never find anything in there. The teacher would say, "Take out your math assignment," and I'd be digging through old dried-up glue sticks, crumpled papers from three weeks ago, half-eaten snacks... it was awful. And because I could never find the assignment, I'd get a zero, even if I actually did it. 

And it wasn't just losing things, either. I was always rushing through everything. Like, if we had a worksheet, I would just glance at the directions and start doing it, and then I'd get half the answers wrong because I didn't actually read what we were supposed to do. I just wanted to be done with it so I could move on to something else. And I was always getting in trouble for talking out of turn, too. I just couldn't hold my thoughts in. If something popped into my head, I had to say it right that second, even if the teacher was right in the middle of a sentence. It was like I physically couldn't wait. So yeah, this isn't just a post-college thing. It's just that now, instead of getting a bad grade for losing a worksheet, I'm losing job opportunities and getting late fees, you know? It just has much bigger consequences now.
Do you still notice things like feeling restless, fidgety, or blurting out things impulsively now as an adult, or has that particular part faded while the forgetfulness/disorganization remained?

Oh, no, it definitely hasn't faded at all. Honestly, if anything, it almost feels worse now just because as an adult, you know, you're expected to just sit perfectly still and be professional and composed, and I just... I really can't. It's this intense, physical thing. Like, when I have to sit through an interview—which is already stressful enough, right?—or a meeting, or honestly even something that's supposed to be fun, like sitting through a movie at the theater, I start feeling this crazy pressure building up inside my body. 

It literally feels like I need to get up, or shift around, or do something with my hands right that exact second, or I am going to completely crawl out of my skin. It's like this trapped energy. If I'm at the movies, I'm always that person who is constantly crossing and uncrossing my legs, or shredding the napkin from the concession stand into tiny little pieces, or playing with the straw in my drink, or getting up to go to the bathroom even if I don't actually have to go, just because the act of sitting in one place for two hours feels like actual torture to me. 

And in professional settings, like the few interviews I have managed to actually make it to, it's so exhausting because I know I need to look calm, but under the desk, I'm bouncing my leg so hard the floor is practically vibrating, or I'm twisting my rings around and around, or digging my nails into my palms. The internal feeling of just desperately needing to move hasn't gone away at all. I just spend a lot of energy trying to hide it now so people don't think I'm weird or not paying attention, but the pressure is always right there.
